title: This Guangzhou Pagoda Looks 9 Floors — Inside It Hides 17 | China Travel Expert
description:
It looks like a nine-story pagoda. Step inside and you'll count seventeen.

Guangzhou's Flower Pagoda, at the Temple of the Six Banyan Trees (Liurong Temple), was built in 1097 and rises 57.6m — the tallest and oldest surviving landmark in a city that's over 2,000 years old. From outside it appears to have nine levels, but hidden mezzanine floors sit between each pair, making seventeen layers in all. The temple itself dates to AD 537 and is one of the early homes of Chinese Chan (Zen) Buddhism. Around the year 1100 the great Song poet Su Dongpo (Su Shi) passed through, saw six banyan trees at the gate, and wrote the characters "Liu Rong" (Six Banyans) — and the temple has carried that name ever since. The colorful painted eaves are why locals nicknamed it the "Flower Pagoda."

🧭 Expert Tip: Climb it right when the gate opens. The internal staircase is narrow and single-file, and it clogs with tour groups by mid-morning.
